message.content:
The sea usually looks **blue**—but its hue can shift all over the spectrum depending on conditions:

| Factor | Effect on Color |
|--------|----------------|
| **Depth & water composition** | Deeper waters absorb longer wavelengths (red/orange) more strongly, leaving shorter‑wavelength light (blue/green). Shallow, sandy bottoms reflect greenish tones. |
| **Clarity / suspended particles** | Clear water scatters less light → deeper blues. Turbid water reflects more white/lightness, giving a milky or gray appearance. |
| **Sun angle & time of day** | Early morning/evening sun gives warm pinks/red hues; midday sun produces vivid turquoise or azure shades. |
| **Algae/floating plants** | Green tint from phytoplankton blooms. |
| **Ice/snow cover** | White or pale blue when ice melts into seawater. |

So while “sea” often conjures images of deep cobalt or bright turquoise, the actual color depends largely on how much light penetrates, what’s dissolved or floating inside, and where you’re looking!
